title: Nominal GDP and the GDP deflator in Country Z: real GDP, output growth and prices
scenario: Country Z, an invented country, reports its nominal GDP and its GDP deflator. Year 1 is the base year.

stimulus.title: Nominal GDP and the GDP deflator in Country Z

table.caption: Country Z, Year 1 is the base year (nominal GDP in billions of dollars; invented data for practice)

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate Country Z's real GDP in Year 2. Show your work.

rubric.point: 480 billion dollars, with work shown: 600 / 125 x 100

parts.sample: Real GDP is nominal GDP divided by the deflator, times 100: $\frac{600}{125} \times 100 = 480$ billion dollars.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Did Country Z's output of goods and services increase, decrease or stay the same from Year 1 to Year 2? Explain using your answer to part A.

rubric.point: Decreased, because real GDP fell from 500 (Year 1, the base year, where real equals nominal) to 480, even though nominal GDP rose
accept: Decreased, because real GDP fell from 500 to 480
Decreased, with a real GDP consistent with the answer to part A that is below 500

parts.sample: Output decreased. In the base year real GDP equals nominal GDP, 500 billion, and real GDP in Year 2 is 480 billion. Nominal GDP rose only because prices rose 25%; the quantity of output fell.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Calculate the inflation rate from Year 1 to Year 2, measured by the GDP deflator. Show your work.
parts.sample: The inflation rate is the percent change in the deflator: $\frac{125 - 100}{100} \times 100 = 25\%$.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: In Year 3, Country Z's nominal GDP is 660 billion dollars and its real GDP is 550 billion dollars. Calculate the GDP deflator for Year 3. Show your work.

rubric.point: 120, with work shown: 660 / 550 x 100 (an index number, not a percent or dollars)

parts.sample: The GDP deflator is nominal GDP divided by real GDP, times 100: $\frac{660}{550} \times 100 = 120$.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Based on your answer to part D, identify whether Country Z had inflation, disinflation or deflation from Year 2 to Year 3. Explain.

rubric.point: Deflation, because the deflator fell (from 125 to 120 or to the value found in part D), so prices fell on average
accept: Deflation, because the price index decreased
An answer consistent with a part D deflator compared with 125

parts.sample: Country Z had deflation. The GDP deflator fell from 125 in Year 2 to 120 in Year 3, so the prices of the goods and services in GDP fell on average (by 4%).
